questions.subject: social
questions.text: The policy of Subsidiary Alliance weakened the native rulers. How?

answer.value: Under the conditions of the Subsidiary Alliance the native rulers were weakened because: the Indian kings had to keep the British army in their kingdom and bear the expenses of the army and the wages of soldiers (or give revenue lands); the king had to have a British Resident in his court; the king could not appoint any other European or enter into any agreement with another Indian state without the permission of the Governor General. In return the Company offered protection, but these conditions robbed the rulers of their independence.

answer_provenance.basis: Textbook 10th English  SS  Part - 1 2026-27(Part 1), pdf p27 (printed p14): "The Conditions of Subsidiary Alliance: 1. The Indian Kings had to keep the British Army in their kingdom. 2. The state concerned had to bear the expenses of the army and the wages of soldiers, or had to give certain revenue lands. 3. The King had to have a British Resident in his Court. 4. The King could not appoint any other European without the permission of the British. 5. ... the permission of the Governor General was mandatory. 6. In return ... the Company would offer protection.". The MQP prints no answer key; answer sourced from the textbook per review_policy_v1 §2-4.

answer_evidence.text: The Conditions of Subsidiary Alliance: 1. The Indian Kings had to keep the British Army in their kingdom. 2. The state concerned had to bear the expenses of the army and the wages of soldiers, or had to give certain revenue lands. 3. The King had to have a British Resident in his Court. 4. The King could not appoint any other European without the permission of the British. 5. ... the permission of the Governor General was mandatory. 6. In return ... the Company would offer protection.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: What are the difference between Kharif and Rabi crops season?

answer.value: Kharif crops are the south-west monsoon crops: they are sown at the beginning of the south-west monsoon (June–July) and harvested at its end — for example paddy. Rabi crops are the north-east monsoon (winter) crops: the seeds are sown in October–November and the crops are harvested during February–March in the cool temperate climate — for example wheat.

answer_provenance.basis: Textbook 10th English  SS  Part - 2 2026-27(Part 2), pdf p86 (printed p84): "1. South-west monsoon or kharif crops 2. North-east monsoon or rabi crops 3. Summer or jade crops. ... Wheat is the most important ‘rabi’ crop ... The seeds are sown in October - November and the crops are harvested during February and March.". The MQP prints no answer key; answer sourced from the textbook per review_policy_v1 §2-4.

answer_evidence.text: 1. South-west monsoon or kharif crops 2. North-east monsoon or rabi crops 3. Summer or jade crops. ... Wheat is the most important ‘rabi’ crop ... The seeds are sown in October - November and the crops are harvested during February and March.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: The unification of Jammu and Kashmir with India is unique compared to that of other provinces. Justify

answer.value: King Harisingh of Jammu and Kashmir first wanted to remain independent. Fearing a merger of Kashmir with India, Pakistan incited the tribals; the National Conference of Sheikh Abdullah, which fought for the freedom of Kashmir, decided that merging with India (which had a democratic republican constitution) was better than merging with Pakistan (which had a religious constitution). Pressurized by these circumstances, Harisingh requested help from the Indian government, and after the Pakistani attempt failed, Jammu and Kashmir merged with India with certain conditions — one part of Kashmir remaining with Pakistan — which makes its unification unique.

answer_provenance.basis: Textbook 10th English  SS  Part - 2 2026-27(Part 2), pdf p33 (printed p31): "King Harisingh of Jammu and Kashmir wanted to remain independent. Fearing a merger of Kashmir with India, Pakistan incited the tribals ... The National Conference of Sheikh Abdullah ... finally decided that merging with India that had a democratic republican constitution, was better than merging with Pakistan ... king Harisingh requested help from the Indian government. After the Pakistani attempt failed, Jammu and Kashmir merged with India with certain conditions. One part of Kashmir remained with Pakistan.". The MQP prints no answer key; answer sourced from the textbook per review_policy_v1 §2-4.

answer_evidence.text: King Harisingh of Jammu and Kashmir wanted to remain independent. Fearing a merger of Kashmir with India, Pakistan incited the tribals ... The National Conference of Sheikh Abdullah ... finally decided that merging with India that had a democratic republican constitution, was better than merging with Pakistan ... king Harisingh requested help from the Indian government. After the Pakistani attempt failed, Jammu and Kashmir merged with India with certain conditions. One part of Kashmir remained with Pakistan.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: Government of India act of 1935 acted as the base for the formation of Indian constitution. Justify.

answer.value: In 1935 the Government of India Act was promulgated. This act had provisions for an Indian Union and provincial independence (autonomy), and through it Indians got political rights. Because of this act, the Congress and the Muslim League participated in elections, the Congress won and formed provincial governments. These provisions of federation, provincial autonomy and political rights became the base for the formation of the Indian Constitution.

answer_provenance.basis: Textbook 10th English  SS  Part - 2 2026-27(Part 2), pdf p18 (printed p16): "in 1935, the Indian Government Act was promulgated. This act had provisions for an Indian Union and provincial independence. Indians got political rights. Due to this, the Congress and Muslim League participated in elections. The Congress won the elections and formed a provincial government.". The MQP prints no answer key; answer sourced from the textbook per review_policy_v1 §2-4.

answer_evidence.text: in 1935, the Indian Government Act was promulgated. This act had provisions for an Indian Union and provincial independence. Indians got political rights. Due to this, the Congress and Muslim League participated in elections. The Congress won the elections and formed a provincial government.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: The role of Satya Shodhaka samaj in reforming the Indian society is ever remembered. Substantiate.

answer.value: The Satyashodhak Samaj, founded by Jyotiba Phule, worked for social justice and equality. It began struggles on behalf of farmers and condemned the exploitation of the shudras (Phule wrote about this exploitation in his book ‘Ghulamagiri’). Through the Satyashodhak Samaj, Phule and his wife Savitribai Phule worked hard for women’s education and started a hostel for girls. Their effort to establish a new society on the principles of equality was important, and it later influenced Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: Explain the economic and military causes for the first war of Indian independence?

answer.value: Economic causes: due to the industrial revolution in England, Indian handicrafts and cottage industries suffered heavily and craftsmen became unemployed; the British imposed a heavy tax on the sale of Indian goods; under the zamindari system landlords exploited the farmers; and the ‘Inam Commission’ took back the gifted (Inam) lands, insulting their holders. questions.subject: social
questions.text: Explain the fundamental principles of foreign policy of India.

answer.value: The principles of Indian foreign policy are: (1) opposition to colonialism; (2) opposition to imperialism; (3) opposition to racial discrimination (apartheid); (4) the policy of non-alignment — after 1945 India remained neutral without joining either power bloc; and (5) priority for the progress of African and Asian countries so that colonised countries come into the mainstream of development.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: How are the Organized sector workers different from Unorganized sector workers?

answer.value: Organised workers are those working in specific fields governed by legal rules and regulations; in the organized sector there is an organizational hierarchy, work is subject to specific terms, transactions are recorded in writing, and workers get fixed wages, allowances, paid leave, pension, medical facilities and specific hours of work (e.g. workers in insurance companies, educational institutions, banks, armed forces, private companies and government departments). Unorganised workers are people who work in areas not governed by specific rules, regulations or unions and earn daily wages; the unorganized sector is very vast and not under government control (e.g. domestic servants, construction workers, agricultural labourers, footpath hawkers, vehicle repairers and push-cart vendors).

questions.subject: social
questions.text: The rule of Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV made Mysore as ‘Modern state’ Justify

answer.value: During the rule of Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV (1894–1940), many developmental works were carried out that made Mysore a modern state: reforms in the gold mines, establishment of colleges, construction of the Marikanive reservoir, railways and hospitals, and a hydro-electric project across the Cauvery at Shivanasamudra. Electricity was supplied to the Kolar Gold Fields and to Bangalore — in fact Bangalore became the first city to be electrified in India. These industrial, educational and infrastructural achievements justify calling Mysore a ‘Modern state’ under him.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: What are the salient features of important soil found in Deccan Trap region?

answer.value: The important soil of the Deccan Trap region is Black soil (also called Regur soil or Black Cotton soil). Its salient features are: it is formed from the weathering of igneous rock; it contains more clay particles; it is fertile and capable of retaining water; it is rich in lime and magnesium carbonates; it is best suited for cotton cultivation and highly suitable for dry farming; and crops such as cotton, jowar, wheat, onion, chilli, tobacco, oil seeds, lemon and grapes are grown in it. It is found in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, western Andhra Pradesh and north Karnataka.

It is fertile and capable of retaining water. ... This soil is more of lime and magnesium carbonates. It is highly suitable for dry farming. Cotton, jowar, wheat, onion, chilli, tobacco, oil seeds, lemon and grapes are the major crops growing in this soil.". questions.subject: social
questions.text: Many factors are influenced the location of sugar industry in India. Justify.

answer.value: The sugar industry is located in the sugarcane-growing areas because sugarcane is a bulky and perishable raw material. The maximum number of sugar industries are located in the Ganga river plain region, and they are found in Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. Uttar Pradesh has the maximum number of sugar mills and is called the ‘Java of India’. Thus nearness to the raw material (sugarcane) is the main factor influencing the location of the sugar industry.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: Explain the contributions of Nehru as a Prime minister of India

answer.value: Jawaharlal Nehru took over as the first Prime Minister of the country. As Prime Minister he laid the foundations of modern India: under his leadership India adopted planned economic development — the first Five-Year Plan came into effect on 1st April 1951 through the National Planning Commission — and he promoted industrialisation and scientific development. In foreign affairs he shaped India’s foreign policy based on non-alignment, keeping India neutral between the power blocs after 1945, and on the principles of anti-colonialism and world peace.
